$comment: Buckets are COMPATIBILITY CLASSES, not namespaces. A bucket directory never appears in a skill's installed path — scripts/build-skills.mjs flattens buckets into the distribution targets listed here. Renaming a bucket directory without updating this file is a hard build error, which is the point: fan-out is declared, never inferred from a folder name. LAYOUT: a bucket holds one subfolder per claude-plugin route key, and the skills sit inside those — bucket/plugin/skill. That subfolder exists so plugin membership is legible in the tree; it is never used to DERIVE routing, which stays declared in targets["claude-plugin"].routes below. Since it makes one fact spelled twice, the build binds the two: a skill whose subfolder is not the route that claims it, a subfolder that is not a route key, and a skill sitting directly under a bucket in the old flat layout are each a hard build error.

pure-prose.description: Universally compatible. Prose only: no tool names, no bundled scripts, no harness-specific assumptions. Runs on any agent that can read text.

claude-code.description: Claude Code only. May bundle scripts, name Claude Code tools, and assume the ~/.claude layout (projects/, memory directories, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules). Runs nowhere else without adaptation.

claude-personal.note: Per-skill link back to the bucket source, so the repo stays the sole source of truth.

claude-rules.note: Per-skill link back to the bucket source, the same shape as claude-personal — the repo stays the sole source of truth. The link is to the skill's DIRECTORY, not to SKILL.md: on Windows this is a directory junction, which cannot link a file, and the directory holds exactly one file, so exactly that file loads.
claude-rules.$comment: WHY A RULES ENTRY EXISTS AT ALL: installed is not loaded. A skill under ~/.claude/skills loads only when it is invoked or judged relevant; a file under ~/.claude/rules loads into context in EVERY session. developer-friendliness was installed as a skill the whole time and did nothing until someone typed its name, and the ruling (#94, 2026-09-10) is that the whole skill loads every session. MEMBERSHIP IS DECLARED, never inferred: buckets[].targets says which compatibility class MAY have a rules entry, and the per-skill list below says who actually gets one — the same declared-not-derived rule as targets["claude-plugin"].routes. A name here that no bucket holds, or whose bucket does not declare this target, is a hard build error. This list is deliberately not everything in the claude-code bucket: every entry adds its bytes to every session, forever.

claude-plugin.note: Staged into <route path>/skills, committed rather than generated-at-install: plugins arrive by git clone with no build step. Each route key IS the trigger prefix and is checked against that plugin's .claude-plugin/plugin.json name.
claude-plugin.$comment: ROUTES, not a single path. A bucket is a compatibility class, not a destination, so it cannot say WHICH plugin a skill ships in — the moment a second plugin draws from the same bucket, a path alone is ambiguous. Routing is therefore declared per skill rather than derived, and stays declared while only one route exists: every skill in a plugin-targeting bucket must appear under exactly one route, and unlisted, listed twice, or listed-but-absent-from-every-bucket are each a hard build error. Same rule as bucket fan-out — declared, never inferred.
